items.title: One Nation, One Election: DMK's P Wilson defends JPC proposal to meet Supreme Court judges
items.summary: The meeting proposed by Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the One Nation, One Election Bills with Supreme Court judges was done based on a proposal by Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party MP, JPC member and Senior Advocate P Wilson. The proposed meeting was called off amid objections over the propriety of sitting judges discussing legislation that could later come before the Court for judicial review. However, Wilson has now defended the proposal for such a meeting. "Unfortunately, due to political objections surrounding this meeting, it was decided to call off the meeting because of unnecessary and unfortunate circumstances caused by vested interests," said Wilson in his statement. The JPC is chaired by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP PP Chaudhary. It had proposed an interaction with Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and other Supreme Court judges. The meeting was part of the JPC's consultations on the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024. items.title: What the Gujarat lawyers’ protest reveals about our democracy
items.summary: For the last few days, lawyers across the State of Gujarat have been up in arms against the Rent Control Bill, 2026 (here “up in arms” is used metaphorically, lest the State government rely on this post to slam sedition and UAPA cases against the protesting lawyers or, much worse, the author). Although this post briefly addresses the causes of concern in the proposed Bill, the main aim of this post is to address the assurance advanced by the Advocate General (AG) to the effect that the Bill will never see the light of the day . This post explores, through the assurance advanced by the AG, the reality of the relationship between the State government and the Governor - a topic which has received considerable engagement from constitutional lawyers as well as courts in the recent past. Why are the lawyers protesting? The protest is directed against the Rent Control Bill, 2026, which seeks to take away the jurisdiction of small causes courts to decide rent disputes and instead vests the revenue authorities such as mamlatdar or deputy collector with the jurisdiction to decide these disputes. items.title: NCLT orders winding up of 14 Popular Finance-linked entities; asks liquidator to trace money, recover assets
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) at Kochi has ordered the winding up of 14 entities linked to the Popular Finance Group and directed the liquidators to trace money collected from the public and identify assets acquired using such funds. A Bench of Judicial Member Vinay Goel and Technical Member Ravichandran Ramasamy passed the batch of orders on October 6 on petitions moved by the Union government through the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO). The 14 entities comprise companies and limited liability partnerships belonging to the Popular Finance Group. The tribunal issued substantially similar directions in the winding-up proceedings and asked liquidators to examine the SFIO investigation report and determine where money collected from members of the public ultimately went. “ Examine the SFIO Investigation Report and other material available on record and trace the flow and end-use of funds collected from the public, ” the tribunal ruled. items.title: Kerala High Court comes to aid of principal denied entry to school for wearing churidar
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently directed the police to ensure that a headmistress of a high school in Kottarakkara is allowed to enter the educational institution freely after she was allegedly stopped at the gate for wearing a churidar [Sindhu S Nair v Secretary, General Education Department & ors] Justice PV Kunhikrishnan said that a person's choice of attire cannot be dictated by another person or by societal customs unless such a restriction has the backing of law. The Court emphasised that when such dictates are issued against the individual choices of a citizen, it is the duty of the law-enforcing authority to take appropriate legal steps. " What dress one wears is ordinarily a matter of personal choice of every citizen of this country. No one or society as a whole can dictate how a citizen should dress without the backing of the law. This is a part of the fundamental rights of every citizen, " the Court said. It added that clothes are an expression of culture, comfort, and individual choice which cannot be used to measure a person's worth or dignity. items.title: P&H High Court initiates contempt case against The Hindu, Dainik Bhaskar over Dera Sacha Sauda propaganda ads
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has initiated suo motu contempt of court proceedings against the editors-in-chief and publishers of The Hindu and Dainik Bhaskar for publishing Dera Sacha Sauda advertisements claiming that its chief, Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh, was being targeted as part of a conspiracy. The matter was today listed before a bench of Justice Vinod S Bhardwaj and Justice Ravinder Malik . The Court listed it for consideration on November 25. Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh is currently serving a 20-year sentence for raping his two disciples. His appeal challenging the conviction and sentence is pending before the High Court. The High Court in 2024 and in March this year had acquitted him in two different murders cases. On September 12, the newspapers published a front-page advertisement which claimed that there was a conspiracy against Ram Rahim. The Hindu later issued a public apology for publishing the advertisement following public backlash. The issue has now got revived in view of the suo motu contempt proceedings initiated on an order passed by Justice Subhas Mehla who said the newspaper advertisements insinuated that courts were a party to the alleged conspiracy. items.title: CJI Surya Kant to attend NLSIU convocation on October 17
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant will attend the 34th annual convocation of the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru on October 17. The convocation will be held from 11 am to 1 pm at the Jnana Jyoti Auditorium on Palace Road, Bengaluru. Justice Kant, who is the Chancellor of NLSIU, will preside over the ceremony, the University said in an invitation circulated to invitees. The convocation comes after NLSIU had earlier cancelled the ceremony scheduled for September 12 after issuing a notice announcing that no convocation would be held for the 2026 batch due to "unavoidable circumstances" and that students would be conferred their degrees in absentia. The cancellation came amid a controversy over the proposed presence of CJI Kant and Bar Council of India (BCI) Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra at the ceremony. More than 700 current students, graduating students and alumni had objected to their participation. The development followed a separate controversy at NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, where students had opposed the proposed presence of CJI Kant at their convocation. items.summary: Sixteen years after he was accused of demanding a ₹5,000 bribe, and long after he finished serving his four-year prison sentence, a former Jharkhand government employee was recently acquitted by the Supreme Court in a corruption case [ Ajit Kumar v. State of Jharkhand ]. A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar set aside the conviction of the appellant, one Ajit Kumar, holding that the prosecution failed to prove the demand and acceptance of any bribe. Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar Notably, when the top court first took up his plea on July 24, 2026, Kumar had already undergone the entire four-year rigorous imprisonment term and paid the ₹10,000 fine earlier imposed on him. However, his counsel informed the Court that Kumar wished to fight the appeal to its logical conclusion to clear his name and remove the institutional stigma attached to a corruption conviction. The case dates back to April 2010, when a school orderly alleged that Kumar - then working in the District Education Office at Saraikella - demanded money to release his pending salary. items.title: Supreme Court closes Constitution Bench reference case on legislative privilege and free speech
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday closed a 2003 case referred to a Constitution Bench to examine the limits of legislative privilege and its interplay with free speech [ N Ravi and others v. Speaker, Legislative Assembly, Chennai and others ]. The Court decided to close the case in view of the fact that the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly had recalled the resolution based on which the case came to be initiated. Therefore, a seven-judge Constitution Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Aravind Kumar, Prashant Kumar Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul M Pancholi, Shree Chandrashekhar and V Mohana closed the matter as infructuous. The Court clarified that the larger questions of law raised in the case remain open but can be examined in future in appropriate proceedings. " The writ petitions are disposed of as having become infructuous. However, the questions of law are kept open to be pursued in future in appropriate proceedings," the Court said. items.title: Supreme Court upholds interim bail to Congress Nandigram candidate Milan Pradhan
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to interfere with a Calcutta High Court order granting interim bail to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan in six criminal cases, to enable him to contest the Nandigram Assembly bypoll. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana added that it is not expressing any comment on the merits of the matter, and that the State is free to contest any future application made by Pradhan to extend his bail period. "We are informed the polling is over for the same and voting took place yesterday and counting is on October 9. The cases indicate certain serious offences but the exact idea of the order is to contest elections and take part in counting and surrender on October 21. In such circumstances, we don't deem to intervene in the impugned judgment. If (an) application is made for extension of bail or made into regular bail, then all contentions of State shall remain open. No opinion expressed on merits," the Court said. items.title: Banks can't unilaterally reduce interest on fixed deposits maintained pursuant to court orders: Delhi High Court
items.summary: Banks cannot unilaterally reduce interest on fixed deposits maintained pursuant to court orders without justification, the Delhi High Court recently held [ Natwest Vs Hero Exports ]. A bench of Justices Avneesh Jhingan and Shail Jain passed a ruling to this effect while dismissing an appeal by NatWest Markets PLC against an order requiring it to pay higher interest on a ₹5.89 crore fixed deposit that was being maintained during the pendency of an arbitration dispute. Justice Avneesh Jhingan The dispute arose between Hero Exports and Tiffins Barrytes, Asbestos and Paints Limited. Before arbitration proceedings commenced, Hero Exports moved the High Court under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act seeking interim protection. In July 2008, the High Court ordered that ₹8.5 crore lying in Tiffins Barrytes' bank accounts be secured. Of this, ₹5.89 crore was lying with ABN Amro Bank, which later became Royal Bank of Scotland and is now NatWest Markets PLC. The Court subsequently directed that the ₹5.89 crore be kept in a fixed deposit yielding the maximum rate of interest.
